Panthers vs. Lions picks, prediction, player props: Expert's NFL Week 4 best bets for Sunday Night Football Targeting a high-scoring shootout in Charlotte, our betting picks back Jahmyr Gibbs in the passing game and Darren Waller to stay heavily involved By Will Brinson Oct 4, 2026 at 7:01 pm ET • 3 min read Add CBS Sports on Google Imagn Images The NFL returns to Charlotte for a Sunday night prime-time game for the first time in more than a decade, and with the Lions coming to town to face the Panthers , we should be in store for some fireworks. Detroit is a 3.5-point favorite in the latest Lions vs. Panthers odds from DraftKings Sportsbook, and the Over/Under on the game total is set at 47.5 points. Bet on Sunday Night Football at DraftKings, where new users get $150 in bonus bets after they spend $5+: One major downside for the Panthers is that they have been ravaged by injuries recently, including losing their best offensive lineman, Damien Lewis , for a while. They also placed both starting cornerbacks on IR, so things could be dicey against this explosive Lions offense. Get a $55 bonus after $25 in trades by claiming the latest Kalshi promo code CBSSPORTS55 here : Best bets for Sunday Night Football Over 51.5 This line has climbed a full point over the last 24 hours, and that probably involves the weather. It was supposed to dump rain all day Sunday in North Carolina, but we're now staring down just some chill in the air and what should be a fun one. The Lions' last appearance in prime time cashed everyone out with the explosive matchup against the Bills . I'm not expecting Carolina to perform like Buffalo did, but the Panthers are highly susceptible to being dragged into shootouts if their opponent starts to sling the ball around. Given the dearth of defensive backfield talent out there for Carolina, I fully expect the Lions to take advantage and throw the ball downfield. Carolina should be able to answer and we should get points galore. Sunday Night Football player props Darren Waller Over 36.5 receiving yards (-112, DraftKings) Bryce Young is going to be forced to pass the ball in this one, and that should bode well for Waller, who's been a surprisingly impressive target for the Panthers as a late addition to the roster. He broke out in Week 2 with a pair of scores then was rewarded with eight targets in Week 3 against the Browns . I'd expect him to see close to that many again Sunday night, making this number just way too low for how much Bryce looks his way, especially if Jalen Coker ends up inactive tonight. Jahmyr Gibbs Over 37.5 receiving yards (-115, DraftKings) Gibbs is the unquestioned best running back in football right now and has really rewarded anyone who took him first overall in fantasy. But he's not just a great runner, he's also an elite receiver, and in a game that should be a shootout with Jared Goff looking to exploit the Panthers defense, I'd expect Gibbs to be plenty involved in the pass game as well. 40 receiving yards feels very, very doable for the superstar. Bet on NFL player props and more at BetMGM: Sunday Night Football anytime touchdowns Jameson Williams (+200, DraftKings) If Williams wasn't having such a meh year so far, this number wouldn't be north of 2-1. But he's been just OK thus far, and as such we're getting a great price. Jamo can score from anywhere, should get plenty of short-yardage looks with screens and the like and also is the ultimate deep threat going against a really depleted secondary. Brycen Tremayne (+360, DraftKings) This is a bit of a longshot, but, again, we're thinking Jalen Coker won't play in this game. That's going to likely slide Tremayne into a starting role opposite of Tetairoa McMillan at wide receiver, and if this is a shootout, Young is going to have to throw a lot. There's a good chance Tremayne gets lost in the sauce near the end zone, setting him up as a nice high-value play to score. White includes Jeremiyah Love, wide receiver totals and the defending Super Bowl champions in his 2026 NFL Draft prop picks ahead of the first round on April 23 By Owen OBrien Apr 20, 2026 at 2:55 pm ET • 5 min read Add CBS Sports on Google Imagn Images The first round of the 2026 NFL Draft is Thursday, April 23, at 8 p.m. ET, and the NFL Draft has turned into a monstrous event in recent years. With a massive NFL event comes numerous NFL betting opportunities for online sports betting . Fernando Mendoza is the overwhelming favorite to be selected No. 1 overall by the Las Vegas Raiders, but there are plenty of other DraftKings NFL Draft props than simply who gets selected first. Betting apps have plenty of 2026 NFL Draft props on individual players, positions and teams for prop betting on the NFL Draft. SportsLine NFL expert R.J. White has locked in some of his best bets for the 2026 NFL Draft at DraftKings, including picking star running back Jeremiyah Love, from Notre Dame, to be one of the first four picks in the NFL Draft 2026. White has locked in his five favorite DraftKings NFL Draft prop picks ahead of the opening round on April 23rd. Check them out below. For NFL Draft betting, new users can take advantage of the latest sign-up bonus at DraftKings. Check out our DraftKings promo code review now to see the newest offer and get started. NFL Draft predictions to target Ravens draft offensive lineman first (+130) The offensive line was a major issue for Baltimore last year, and it hasn't gotten any better with Tyler Linderbaum leaving for Las Vegas. Whether it's moving up a bit for Francis Mauigoa or Spencer Fano, taking a plug-and-play interior lineman like Olaivavega Ioane, or even selecting Kadyn Proctor as the heir apparent at left tackle, the Ravens should be using a draft like this that isn't considered stacked with blue-chip talent to stock up on help to address their biggest weakness. We saw a little shift from our initial recommendation to play this at +140 last week, but I believe it should be even odds at least. Trade NFL Draft props at Kalshi. Check out our Kalshi promo code review to see their latest offers. Carnell Tate draft position: Under 7.5 (-105) The market appears to be predicting a little bit of a slide for Tate after the Ohio State receiver was once considered the clear option for the Browns at No. 6. While I believe Cleveland will go with an offensive lineman at that spot, I don't know that Tate gets by the Commanders at No. 7, particularly if Jeremiyah Love and Sonny Styles go off the board in the top five. Tate would be a great running mate and eventual replacement for Terry McLaurin, and receiver is a clear need for Washington. Getting the underdog side of this market while having the potential to hit with either the Browns or Commanders seems like good value. Rueben Bain drafted before Mansoor Delane (-120) This is a head-to-head matchup available at DraftKings that I could see shifting quickly. Teams don't seem to be too worried about Bain's arm length, and on ability alone he has an argument to be taken in the top five in the same tier as Arvell Reese and David Bailey. Delane is probably the best corner prospect in the draft, though a team comfortable with Jermod McCoy's medicals could prefer him, and there is good enough depth at corner that I don't see Delane as a potential trade-up target like Bain could be. Bain's window could legitimately start at No. 4 overall and I can't see him getting past No. 9, while Delane's window starts at No. 8 and probably goes down to No. 12, unless the Cowboys are one of those McCoy teams. That leaves a small margin for Delane to win this matchup. Check out our bet365 bonus code review right now and get their latest sign-up promo. NFL Draft longshot picks Seahawks draft running back first (+380) The defending Super Bowl champions lost their Super Bowl MVP, and White thinks they may turn to the NFL Draft to replace him. The Seahawks declined to franchise tag or re-sign Kenneth Walker III after he rushed for 135 yards in Seattle's 29-13 Super Bowl win over the Patriots. Whether it's with the final pick in the first round or by trading back, White expects Seattle to prioritize a replacement. "No. 32 might be a little high for Jadarian Price, but I think there's a good chance the Seahawks are taking him with their first pick in a different spot," White said. "Running back is their clearest need with Kenneth Walker gone and Zach Charbonnet injured, and we saw how big an impact the rushing attack had in the Super Bowl last year. Seattle has just four picks and will likely prioritize adding more on Draft Day, and those late first-round picks are key for those looking to trade up (maybe for Ty Simpson?) as they come with a fifth-year option. I see the Seahawks making a trade back, then selecting Price in Round 2." Claim the latest BetMGM bonus code. Check out our BetMGM bonus code review now and get it. Jacob Rodriguez drafted in Round 1 (+380) With this draft class being perceived as short on top-tier talent, there is the potential for the back half of the first round to look even more different from consensus mock drafts than recent years. I see logic in examining the Round 1 pick market as a result for longshots we can take a chance on, and Rodriguez fits the bill. He and CJ Allen play a non-premium position at off-ball linebacker but have high floors and reasons to believe each could land in Round 1, especially to teams looking for a piece to come in and make an immediate impact. Rodriguez won a lot of hardware for his collegiate performance in 2025, and in particular, I could see a number of teams in the back half of Round 1 having him higher on their boards than we expect. Lions draft safety first (+3000) Brad Holmes is a best-player-available type of drafter, and with offensive lineman a massive -380 favorite in this prop, I see potential to take a big swing on a lottery ticket play. Detroit's pick at No. 17 is in the perfect range to target an excellent safety class that includes Dillon Thieneman (often tied to the Vikings one pick later) or Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, and even though the Lions have one of the best safety pairings in the league when healthy, there are injury concerns around both Kerby Joseph, who reportedly has a serious knee injury that clouds his long-term outlook, and Brian Branch, who tore his Achilles late last season. Accordingly, I predict Lamb clears this line for a fourth straight game. Chris Godwin Over 3.5 Receptions (+115) Godwin enjoyed a higher target share on Sunday against the Packers. By Zachary Cohen - September 26, 2026 83263 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 3 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 3 NFL best bets and Week 3 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts New England Patriots at Jacksonville Jaguars – 1:00 pm ET The Jaguars are coming off a loss last week, but there’s no shame in losing to the Broncos. That was a meeting between two teams that can easily work themselves deep into the AFC playoffs. Denver just so happened to be the home team. Well, Jacksonville will be the home team in this meeting with New England, giving the Jaguars a little bit of an edge. However, beyond that, I currently view them as a better team than the Patriots. It’s very early in the season, but Jacksonville currently resides in Tier 2 when looking at RBSDM’s EPA tiers. New England is barely in Tier 3. The Patriots are undoubtedly a strong defensive team, but very little separates these teams on that side of the ball. The difference between the two is on offense, as the Jaguars have a balanced lineup and an excellent play caller. The Patriots have the latter, along with a talented quarterback, but they’re missing AJ Brown. This is the exact type of game in which that could come back to haunt them. Our VSiN matchup page for this game calls for the Jaguars to win by 3.0. I see it being a little more lopsided than that, but we have -2.5 in case it is decided by a field goal. Bet: Jaguars -2.5 (-120) Tennessee Titans at New York Giants – 1:00 pm ET It might be hard to get on board with backing the Giants without Jaxson Dart, and it’s probably harder considering how poorly Jameis Winston played against the Rams. However, we haven’t seen anything through two weeks that suggests Tennessee is better than New York. The Giants are currently last in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.257), but it’s early enough in the season that each game can really change stats. Well, New York got carved up by Los Angeles in the Sunday Night Football game, and this Titans offense isn’t the Rams offense. I’d be very surprised if Cam Ward can go on the road and deliver a victory — or cover 2.5 points — against a tough team with playoff aspirations. As things stand, the Titans are ranked 20th or worse in both EPA/Play and EPA/Play Allowed. I’m also not too worried about Winston. Sure, last week was absolutely miserable, but his track record as a starter speaks for itself. Honestly, a good argument can be made that he’s the best backup in the league, and a week of reps with the starters should do him wonders. His timing looked off in Week 2, and that should get there as he gets more familiar with his weapons. John Harbaugh has also been outrageously productive in games with lines between +3 and -3. In his career, his teams are 79-53 straight-up and 73-49 against the spread in those games. Bet: Giants -2.5 (-118) Ravens at Cowboys – 4:25 pm ET Henry is averaging 106.0 yards per game through two weeks, and his 144-yard performance against the Colts helped. He absolutely dominated Indianapolis between the tackles, and something tells me he’ll do the same to Dallas. In Week 1, the Cowboys gave up 165 rushing yards against the Giants. Dallas also allowed 182 rushing yards against Washington last week. As of right now, despite all the offseason moves the Cowboys made to address their defense, they’re No. 24 in the NFL in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.003). That’s trouble heading into a meeting with Henry, who can run over defenders up the middle or utilize his quickness to break off a long one. In Henry’s last 11 games against bottom-10 opponents in rushing yards allowed, the future Hall of Famer is averaging 104.1 rushing yards per game. He has also gone Over 85.5 rushing yards in six of the 11. I’ll also note that Henry rushed for 151 yards the last time he played at Jerry World. That was a different defense and venue, but he’ll enjoy the atmosphere in Brazil — and extra eyeballs. Without further ado, here are three of the best player props for NFL Week 1, including Garrett Wilson, David Montgomery and Omarion Hampton. *]:mx-auto lg:[&>*]:mx-0"> Best NFL Player Prop Bets and Picks for Week 1 David Montgomery Anytime TD (-120) David Montgomery has found a new home in Houston. The Lions’ “Sonic and Knuckles” duo in the backfield was one of the best in the league over the past few years. However, Montgomery was always second fiddle to Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit. He was always productive, especially in the red zone, but now he has the chance to be the RB1 for the Texans. Over the past three seasons, Montgomery has scored 33 touchdowns on the ground, despite being in that backup role. Now, he should get almost all of the touches when Houston is in the scoring area. The Bills had an awful run defense last season. They ranked 31st in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 25th in defensive rushing success rate. This Houston team has struggled with pass protection over the past couple of seasons, so it should try to take advantage of that poor run defense and get the ball to Montgomery whenever possible. David Montgomery should start his Houston tenure with a touchdown. Garrett Wilson 6+ Receptions (-121) During the offseason, new Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich described Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall as the Jets’ “bell cows.” The Jets aren’t a great team, but they know they have two very reliable and dangerous weapons in Wilson and Hall. To make things easy on Geno Smith, Reich will want to scheme ways to get the ball to those two players as often as possible. Wilson dealt with an injury that kept him out for most of last season, but in the first six games of the season when he was fit, Wilson had at least six catches in four of those six games. Geno Smith did not have a good season in Las Vegas, but he had a terrible offensive line and a bad group of skill position players. He might not get back to the guy he was in Seattle, but he should have a much better season with an underrated Jets offensive line protecting him. Smith might have turnover issues, but he is not afraid to let it fly. Since the start of the 2022 season, he ranks fourth in the NFL in pass attempts. This Titans defense is very vulnerable, and Frank Reich should let Geno Smith chuck it early and often in this game. Last season, the Titans ranked 29th in the NFL in defensive EPA/pass and 26th in dropback success rate. This is a good early matchup for Smith to get his feet under him in a Jets uniform (for the second time) and feed his WR1 Garrett Wilson. Omarion Hampton Over 68.5 Rushing Yards (-114) This should be a big season for Omarion Hampton. He only played nine games in his rookie season for the Chargers, but he is set for a huge role in what should be a productive Los Angeles offense. This is a good matchup for him to start the season against the Cardinals. Last season, Arizona ranked 22nd in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 23rd in defensive rushing success rate. That defense has a lot of young, inexperienced pieces and should struggle again this season. The Chargers should feed the ball to Hampton early and often to control the game against Arizona. The Chargers are also big favorites and should lead this game down the stretch. That should lead to a lot of carries for Hampton down the stretch while the Chargers put the game on ice. This Houston team has struggled with pass protection over the past couple of seasons, so it should try to take advantage of that poor run defense and get the ball to Montgomery whenever possible. David Montgomery should start his Houston tenure with a touchdown. Garrett Wilson 6+ Receptions (-121) During the offseason, new Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich described Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall as the Jets’ “bell cows.” The Jets aren’t a great team, but they know they have two very reliable and dangerous weapons in Wilson and Hall. To make things easy on Geno Smith, Reich will want to scheme ways to get the ball to those two players as often as possible. Wilson dealt with an injury that kept him out for most of last season, but in the first six games of the season when he was fit, Wilson had at least six catches in four of those six games. Geno Smith did not have a good season in Las Vegas, but he had a terrible offensive line and a bad group of skill position players.

Tool Fantasy Cheat Sheet NFL Player Prop Odds FAQ What Are NFL Player Props? NFL player props are bets on a specific statistical outcome for a specific NFL player. We cover passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards, and anytime touchdowns in our tool, but there are countless other betting opportunities every week. Every prop bet has two parts: The number (Over or Under 81.5 rushing yards, for example) The price, which determines how much a winning bet returns and reflects the implied probability If two players are lined at 45.5 receiving yards, that does not necessarily mean they have the same implied odds. Player A — Over 45.5 receiving yards (-115) — 53.5% implied over probability — Winning $100 bet has $187 return Player B — Over 45.5 receiving yards (+105) — 48.8% implied over probability — Winning $100 bet has $205 return When Do NFL Player Props Come Out Each Week? Some marquee player props are posted earlier in the week, but the majority are released on Wednesday or Thursday after injury reports have been announced. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Check our full list of player props for Week 2 of the 2026 NFL regular season Standout players for my NFL Week 2 player props include Bijan Robinson , Dak Prescott , and Christian McCaffrey Read on to find my full list of NFL Week 2 player props and predictions Welcome to Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season. Early narratives are taking shape, and the slate features a fascinating mix of elite pocket presence, stingy defensive schemes, and enticing volume opportunities. The marquee showdown highlights Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals clashing with C.J. Stroud and the Houston Texans. Meanwhile, Lamar Jackson leads the Baltimore Ravens against Tyler Shough and a clicking New Orleans Saints air raid offense. Evaluating defensive vulnerabilities is critical for identifying value. The Atlanta Falcons’ skill players face a Carolina Panthers defense ranking among the absolute worst following a rough opening performance. Conversely, the Miami Dolphins must grind against a San Francisco 49ers unit already established as formidable. Similarly, the Kansas City Chiefs boast an elite defense equipped to disrupt the visiting Indianapolis Colts. I’m diving into the matchups to uncover the best player prop to bet on for each roster this weekend. Top NFL Week 2 Player Prop Picks and Best Bets Relying on volume projections, red zone efficiency, and underlying trends is the most effective way to identify high-probability outcomes. By evaluating offensive schemes and positional mismatches, we uncover wagers offering the strongest statistical confidence. Here is the single best prop pick for every active team, driven by favorable matchup dynamics and the latest NFL odds . Team Opponent Player Prop Pick (Line & Odds) ARI SEA Jacoby Brissett Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-227) ATL CAR Bijan Robinson Over 4.5 Receptions (-154) BAL NO Derrick Henry Under 1.5 Receptions (-200) CAR ATL Chuba Hubbard Under 2.5 Receptions (-182) CHI MIN Kyle Monangai Under 1.5 Receptions (-200) CIN HOU Evan McPherson Over 1.5 Extra Points (-180) CLE TB Quinshon Judkins Under 2.5 Receptions (-192) DAL WAS Dak Prescott Over 1.5 Passing TDs (-200) DEN JAX Adam Trautman Under 1.5 Receptions (-208) GB NYJ Jordan Love Under 0.5 INTs (-161) HOU CIN Ka’imi Fairbairn Under 2.5 Extra Points (-182) IND KC Daniel Jones Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-278) JAX DEN Cam Little Over 1.5 Extra Points (-189) KC IND Kenneth Walker III Anytime TD Scorer (Yes, -214) LA NYG Kyren Williams Under 2.5 Receptions (-189) LAC LV Omarion Hampton Under 2.5 Receptions (-188) LV LAC Kirk Cousins Over 0.5 Passing TDs (-265) MIA SF Greg Dulcich Under 2.5 Receptions (-189) MIN CHI Will Reichard Over 1.5 Extra Points (-200) NE PIT Andres Borregales Under 2.5 Extra Points (-163) NO BAL Alvin Kamara Under 2.5 Receptions (-200) NYG LA Jaxson Dart Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-222) NYJ GB Geno Smith Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-222) PHI TEN Jalen Hurts Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-189) PIT NE Jaylen Warren Over 2.5 Receptions (-182) SEA ARI Drew Lock Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-222) SF MIA Christian McCaffrey Anytime TD Scorer (Yes, -250) TB CLE Jalen McMillan Under 2.5 Receptions (-197) TEN PHI Gunnar Helm Over 2.5 Receptions (-167) WAS DAL Rachaad White Under 2.5 Receptions (-200) Highlighted Best Bets for NFL Week 2 Daniel Jones (IND) – Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-278) : Facing a capable Chiefs defense, trends suggest the Colts will struggle finishing drives. The heavy juice reflects massive confidence Jones fails to throw multiple scores. Kirk Cousins (LV) – Over 0.5 Passing TDs (-265) : The Las Vegas Raiders are heavily favored to find the end zone through the air against the Los Angeles Chargers. Backing Cousins for a single touchdown pass is an exceptionally strong wager based on projected volume. Christian McCaffrey (SF) – Anytime TD Scorer (-250) : With the 49ers boasting an 88.6% win probability, McCaffrey remains the focal point of a high-powered offense. Heavy workload projections make his goal-line plunge one of the safest sports betting picks on the board. NFL Week 2 Matchups and Prop Analysis Here is the game-by-game breakdown of the best matchups and player props for Week 2 of the 2026 NFL regular season. Panthers vs Falcons Panthers: Chuba Hubbard | Under 2.5 Receptions (-182) Falcons: Bijan Robinson | Over 4.5 Receptions (-154) Panthers enter with a 58.0% win probability over Falcons. Anticipate a ground-and-pound scheme from the visitors if they control the clock, minimizing Hubbard’s target share. Conversely, a 42.0% win probability suggests a negative game script for the hosts, making Robinson an attractive safety valve. Saints vs Ravens Saints: Alvin Kamara | Under 2.5 Receptions (-200) Ravens: Derrick Henry | Under 1.5 Receptions (-200) Ravens act as massive 78.3% home favorites against Saints. Expected to play from ahead, Henry should see a traditional run-heavy workload to salt the game away, suppressing his receiving volume. The visitors face a daunting challenge against a unit equipped to shut down Kamara’s passing-game utilization. (New Orleans probability: 21.7%). Vikings vs Bears Vikings: Will Reichard | Over 1.5 Extra Points Made (-200) Bears: Kyle Monangai | Under 1.5 Receptions (-200) The Chicago Bears carry a 66.8% win probability into this clash against the Minnesota Vikings. Operating as home frontrunners, a run-centric second half caps Monangai’s opportunities. As 33.2% underdogs, Minnesota’s offense still projects to find the end zone enough to make Reichard converting two extra points highly probable. Bengals vs Texans Bengals: Evan McPherson | Over 1.5 Extra Points Made (-180) Texans: Ka’imi Fairbairn | Under 2.5 Extra Points Made (-182) Texans hold a slight 57.1% win probability edge. Despite their 42.9% underdog status, Bengals boast enough offensive firepower to make McPherson an excellent bet for multiple extra points. Playing Fairbairn under his total suggests expectations of tight red zone efficiency or an offensive struggle for the hosts. Steelers vs Patriots Steelers: Jaylen Warren | Over 2.5 Receptions (-182) Patriots: Andres Borregales | Under 2.5 Extra Points Made (-163) The New England Patriots boast a 68.3% win probability. With the Pittsburgh Steelers facing a 31.7% chance to win, Warren should benefit from numerous check-down passes while playing from behind. Fading Borregales aligns with New England’s historically methodical, lower-scoring approach prioritizing the field position battle. Packers vs Jets Packers: Jordan Love | Under 0.5 Interceptions Thrown (-161) Jets: Geno Smith | Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-222) The Green Bay Packers travel as comfortable 62.6% favorites. Operating from strength, Love is projected to exhibit elite pocket presence, avoid mistakes, and win the turnover differential. The New York Jets face a steep 37.4% win probability, making it difficult to envision Smith tossing multiple scores on current NFL passing TD odds . Browns vs Buccaneers Browns: Quinshon Judkins | Under 2.5 Receptions (-192) Buccaneers: Jalen McMillan | Under 2.5 Receptions (-197) The Tampa Bay Buccaneers dominate projections with a 78.7% win probability. Their heavy frontrunner status means they rarely force-feed McMillan late. The Cleveland Browns (21.3%) will struggle to sustain drives, severely limiting Judkins’ chances of securing three or more NFL receptions props . Eagles vs Titans Eagles: Jalen Hurts | Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-189) Titans: Gunnar Helm | Over 2.5 Receptions (-167) The Philadelphia Eagles carry a robust 75.2% win probability on the road. A heavy rushing scheme near the goal line keeps Hurts from throwing for multiple scores. The Tennessee Titans face a significant 24.8% deficit, forcing obvious passing situations that make Helm a fantastic target. Jaguars vs Broncos Jaguars: Cam Little | Over 1.5 Extra Points Made (-189) Broncos: Adam Trautman | Under 1.5 Receptions (-208) The Denver Broncos are 58.4% home favorites. Playing with a projected lead, they will minimize passing volume, directly impacting Trautman’s target share. Even with a 41.6% win probability, the Jacksonville Jaguars possess enough ability to score multiple touchdowns, clearing the path for Little. Raiders vs Chargers Raiders: Kirk Cousins | Over 0.5 Passing TDs (-265) Chargers: Omarion Hampton | Under 2.5 Receptions (-188) Chargers are massive 73.2% favorites. As they dictate tempo, Hampton’s passing game involvement should be minimal. Sitting at a 26.8% win probability guarantees Raiders will throw late into the fourth quarter, making Cousins a premier anchor play. Seahawks vs Cardinals Seahawks: Drew Lock | Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-222) Cardinals: Jacoby Brissett | Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-227) The Seattle Seahawks act as solid 65.3% road favorites over the Arizona Cardinals. Statistical indicators point toward a grinding, low-scoring affair with limited third down conversions. Taking the under on both quarterbacks reflects confidence this matchup will be won in the trenches. (Arizona 34.7% win probability). Commanders vs Cowboys Commanders: Rachaad White | Under 2.5 Receptions (-200) Cowboys: Dak Prescott | Over 1.5 Passing TDs (-200) The Dallas Cowboys enter with a commanding 65.7% win probability. Backing Prescott to throw multiple scores is strong given expected offensive output. The Washington Commanders, heavily overmatched at 34.3%, face immense pressure from the defensive front, short-circuiting the timing needed for White to catch three passes. Dolphins vs 49ers Dolphins: Greg Dulcich | Under 2.5 Receptions (-189) 49ers: Christian McCaffrey | Anytime TD Scorer (Yes, -250) 49ers boast the highest win probability of the weekend at 88.6%. With expectations to dismantle their opponents, McCaffrey finding the end zone is incredibly safe on NFL TD scorer odds . Dolphins stare down an 11.4% probability against an elite defense, leaving Dulcich hard-pressed to find operating room. Colts vs Chiefs Colts: Daniel Jones | Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-278) Chiefs: Kenneth Walker III | Anytime TD Scorer (Yes, -214) Chiefs hold a 71.4% advantage to win at Arrowhead Stadium. Dictating the pace places Walker in a favorable position to punch in a ground score. The 28.6% probability for Colts mirrors expectations that Jones will fail to throw multiple touchdowns against a fierce defense. Giants vs Rams Giants: Jaxson Dart | Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-222) Rams: Kyren Williams | Under 2.5 Receptions (-189) The Los Angeles Rams are firmly in the driver’s seat as 74.7% home favorites. A positive game script allows them to lean heavily on the run, cutting into Williams’ receiving opportunities. The New York Giants hold just a 25.3% win probability, facing a suffocating secondary that severely restricts Dart. He’s been a buzzy late 1st-round pick across several sources (Tony Pauline) and has been tied to several teams between picks 15-32, such as Dallas, Houston, Miami, Buffalo, Pittsburgh, Tampa Bay, New England, and Chicago.” – Andrew Erickson ( FantasyPros ) Who will be the fourth overall pick? “Arvell Reese ( +650 at DraftKings ) or Sonny Styles ( +175 at BetMGM ) — The info/draft rumors I hear about change literally by the minute. By the time you read this, things might be drastically different, but here goes nothing. (FYI- at the time of this writing, it’s Wednesday night, 10:30 p.m.) Anyway, it sounds like Arizona’s owner, Michael Bidwell, might veto GM Monte Ossenfort’s wishes to trade out of the third pick. The rumor is that Ossenfort apparently either wants Edge David Bailey if he’s there or to trade it for more picks if the Jets select Bailey. However, Bidwell wants Jeremiyah Love because he would add some excitement to the Cardinals’ fan base and could help sell some tickets. So, if you think Arizona keeps the pick and selects Love, I think the best way to play that would be to bet the Titans to select Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles. I don’t think Titans’ head coach Robert Saleh (who is a former defensive coordinator) would take Love, Carnell Tate, or Jordyn Tyson over a good prospect on defense, even if he slips. And if Arizona picks Love, you essentially get a free roll with Reese, assuming the Titans don’t trade the pick. Worth a shot.” – Mark Ringo ( Sleepers and Busts ) Carnell Tate drafted in Top 7 ( +105 ) “Carnell Tate’s draft position u7.5 ( +105 at DraftKings ). I’m surprised this bet hasn’t been steamed, but it could be by the time you read this. I’ll grab this bet and take it anywhere I can find it for plus money. Tate’s floor right now looks like seventh overall to the Commanders, and I wouldn’t be shocked if he went as high as fourth overall to the Titans.” – Derek Brown ( FantasyPros ) Fewer than 8.5 SEC players drafted in First Round ( -185 ) “You’ll make money if you bet that there will be fewer than 8.5 players from SEC schools selected in the first round (-185). Normally, the first round of the draft is littered with SEC guys. Not this year. Mansoor Delane (LSU), Kadyn Proctor (Alabama), and Keldric Faulk (Auburn) are the SEC’s only first-round locks, and K.C. Concepcion (Texas A&M) is a near-lock. That’s four. Jermod McCoy (Tennessee), Colton Hood (Tennessee), and Ty Simpson (Alabama) are better than 50/50 to go in the first round, but McCoy’s stock is plummeting due to a worrisome knee issue, and there are only two or three potential first-round suitors for Simpson, none of whom would draft him with the picks they currently hold in the top half of the round. If all of these SEC maybes make it, that’s seven, leaving one SEC player to spare. Chase Bisontis (Texas A&M), Cashius Howell (Texas A&M), Zion Young (Missouri), C.J. Allen (Georgia, and Caleb Banks (Florida) are first-round possibilities. There’s a decent chance one of these players makes it into the first round. I don’t think we’ll see two or more players from this group make it, and if we do get more than one, it could very well be at the expense of McCoy, Hood, or Simpson.” – Pat Fitzmaurice ( FantasyPros ) Carnell Tate to be first WR drafted ( -180 ) “Carnell Tate is the betting favorite to be the first wide receiver selected in the 2026 NFL Draft at -180 odds, largely due to his exceptional route running and ‘pro-ready’ profile. While Jordyn Tyson is hands down the best pure receiver in this class, his extensive injury history, including major knee surgery and a broken collarbone, has dropped him to the second or third receiver off the board on most teams’ lists. NFL front offices are notoriously risk-averse in the top ten, making Tate the safer bet to anchor a professional offense immediately. This shift in draft stock highlights a classic case where reliability outweighs elite but fragile potential. Ultimately, taking Tate at these odds is a play on the certainty of his health and polished Buckeye pedigree over the medical gamble Tyson presents.” – Lawrence Iacona ( Gridiron Experts ) Makai Lemon to be first WR drafted ( +2000 ) “Makai Lemon – 1st Wide Receiver Drafted ( +2000 at Caesars ). I'm going with Makai Lemon as the first wide receiver off the board. Bold, absolutely. Crazy? Maybe, but hear me out. This is often a copycat league. I believe a wide receiver-needy team, such as the New York Giants, might consider Lemon. The Giants already have Malik Nabers, a top outside threat, and could look to replicate what Seattle did with Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Detroit with Amon-Ra St. Brown, using Lemon in a similar role. I'm going with the Giants selecting Lemon at 5, assuming Jeremiyah Love is already off the board.” – Paul Brenton ( EPB1983Dynasty ) Related articles College Football Week 7 Picks: Best Early Bets (2026) NFL Monday Night Football Player Props & Picks: Bills vs. Rams NFL Week 5 Picks, Predictions and Parlays NBA Preseason Picks & Predictions: Monday (10/12) Early NFL Best Bets & Trends for Week 6 (2026) MLB Same Game Parlays & Picks: Monday (10/12) Click to go to homepage NFL Home Odds Picks Matchups Tools Research Articles Teams Leaderboards MLB Home Odds Picks Matchups Tools Research Articles Teams Leaderboards Podcasts NCAAF Home Odds Picks Matchups Tools Leaderboards Articles Teams Podcast Careers Product Updates BettingPros API Get Involved About Us Contact Us Terms of Use Privacy Policy Third Party Licenses Do Not Sell Accessibility Disclosures Affiliate Signup © 2018–2026 BettingPros.com. Many of these fans place wagers on the teams they feel will win those head-to-head matchups. But the NFL is also built upon star power and athletic playmaking—with these exciting moments, come NFL player prop bets, allowing fans to place wagers on their favorite NFL players to perform like superstars. What Are NFL Player Props? NFL player prop bets allow fans to wager on the likelihood that a football star will perform above or below expectations in a specific statistical category, or that they will achieve certain notable events during the game. Like any wager, greater risk means higher payout, so placing a wager on a struggling quarterback to throw for four touchdowns will return stronger odds than a wager on the reigning MVP who has been on a hot streak. Why Bet on NFL Player Props? Player prop bets add a layer of entertainment to your NFL experience. Unlike a head-to-head matchup where you might place your bet and check the score after the game is over, placing wagers on individual achievements and statistics gives you even more reason to watch the game and root for the player you bet on. With a wager on a statistical category, each time that player achieves you are a step closer to a profitable bet, which adds entertainment and excitement to your experience. Just as there are a variety of positions, ways to score, and statistics involved in an NFL game, there are a wide variety of player prop bet options. Whether it is a wager on a favorite player or in a statistical category you love to follow, there is likely a player prop category for every bettor. Most Common NFL Player Prop Bets With so many unique positions and statistics in NFL football, there is just as much variety in the player prop bets available. You can choose over/under bets on passing yards, rushing yards, passing touchdowns, interceptions, and total receptions, depending on your chosen player’s position. If you notice that a receiver with potential is +500 to score a touchdown and you believe he’s due for a breakout game you will profit if the receiver scores a TD. You can also choose head-to-head matchups—for example, you can wager that your favorite quarterback will throw for more passing yards than the quarterback he is matched against in a given week. More NFL Betting Advice NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet Expert NFL Game Picks NFL Betting Strategy Best +EV NFL Picks Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App >> NFL Player Props & Bets: Patriots vs. Seahawks (odds courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook ) Jadarian Price Over 1.5 Receptions ( +124 ) Jadarian Price was not much of a pass-catcher in college, but that will likely change in the NFL. Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury comes from the Kyle Shanahan coaching tree. Christian McCaffrey had a better target share than some of the league's best wide receivers last season. Getting Price on track will be crucial for Seattle’s offense in this game, whether on the ground or in the air. Against the Patriots’ defense, expect it to be harder for him to get on track on the ground in his first taste of NFL action. Last season, Darnold ran for five yards in the Super Bowl and recorded 10+ rushing yards in just four games. But with Kenneth Walker III gone, a rookie running back in his place and a new offensive coordinator, there will be hiccups and growing pains in this game. Consequently, opportunities will arise when the team needs Darnold to make a few plays with his legs. Don’t expect big runs, but 2-4 carries for 10+ yards is reasonable. Hunter Henry Over 3.5 Receptions ( +148 ) Everyone will want to see Drake Maye throwing early and often to his new toys, A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, and he probably will. But when push comes to shove, and he needs a clutch reception to keep a drive moving, look for him to fall back on old reliable - tight end Hunter Henry. Henry had three catches in the Super Bowl and had four or more receptions in nine regular-season games last season. Tight ends saw a lot of success against Seattle’s defense last season, and Henry was one of the best against zone schemes (which the Seahawks often run). Doubs and Brown will be the superstars in the passing game, but Henry is the glue that will move the chains and keep drives moving. highlights: After a shellacking of the Packers by the Falcons on Thursday Night Football, our attention turns to the Sunday main slate and the best NFL Player Props for Week 3. Let's run through a trio of props that the Fantasy Life betting staff is on. Join Our Newsletter Trusted by 400,000+ fantasy football players. Get access to Fantasy Life's free award winning newsletter and tools , all in one step. By registering or logging in, you agree to our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy Geno Smith - o218.5 Passing Yards (-115, bet365) Kody Malstrom: The emergence of Adonai Mitchell has played a major role in Smith’s successful start to the year, giving his QB another reliable pass catcher to throw to while simultaneously pulling defensive attention away from Garrett Wilson When forced to stretch out, the width of Smith’s passing lanes will widen, improving the quality of his throws.

By trimming down on his total number of turnover-worthy plays, Smith will be able to keep the Jets' drives alive, leading to an uptick in his total number of pass attempts to help clear the over on his passing yardage prop. Tyler Allgeier Under 33.5 Receiving Yards (-114; FanDuel) Matt LaMarca: Allgeier may be the starting RB in Arizona, but his hold on that job is tenuous at best. The Cardinals selected Jeremiyah Love with the third overall pick, and you don’t draft a running back that high and keep him on the bench. Allgeier did lead the Cardinals’ RBs in snaps last week, but his rushing share took a step back. He finished with just 31% of the team’s rushing attempts, and he finished with just 10 rushing yards. Allgeier did get to 61 rushing yards in his first game of the season, but he had 17 carries in a game that the Cardinals led throughout. The Cardinals figure to be playing from behind in this contest, and Love’s role should only continue to grow.

Add it all up, and the under with Allgeier has some value. Darren Waller Anytime Touchdown (+340, DraftKings) Justin Carlucci: Darren Waller ’s touchdown number immediately jumps off the page. You can get Waller at +340 to score on DraftKings, and I think there is real value there given how his role has grown from week to week. This did not just appear out of nowhere in the regular season, either. Carolina used Waller in the slot and moved him around during camp, which was a strong indication that the Panthers had plans to involve him near the goal line.

Minnesota Vikings (-2.5) at New Orleans Saints (49.7%) Am I worried that the Vikings "only" beat Miami by five points last week? No. We all saw T.J. Hockenson slide down inside the five-yard line, and if he scores there, the margin is 12 or 13 points as it should have been. Miami was not any point in that game, even if the Vikings didn't blow them out. Minnesota is getting it done with defense and a great kicking game, but their offense is showing some signs of life and could be getting Justin Jefferson back this week. Even if they don't, Kyler Murray is finally settling in, and they have enough weapons to move the ball effectively against a Saints defense that was just blasted by a one-dimensional Atlanta offense. I think the Saints faked us out with their win over the Ravens in Week 2, and their near-win against the Lions looks less impressive now that we've seen Detroit struggle to stop anyone. I like Minnesota to go in and get their fifth win of the year, and all we need is a field goal to cover. Joe Burrow OVER 235.5 Passing Yards (52.6%) Burrow has comfortably cleared this bar in three of four games, with the only time he went under in Week 2, when Cincy played from well out in front against Houston. We don't know which receivers he will have at his disposal, but we do know that he has one of the top matchups on the board as the Dolphins rank near the bottom of the league in every pass defense metric. They've allowed three straight QBs from run-first offenses (Mahomes, Purdy, Murray) to go clear this bar. The Bengals have not run the ball all that effectively, so I expect Burrow to have to throw the ball enough to go over this number. Whether it's Chase Brown out of the backfield, Mike Gesicki in the slot, or even Dohnte Meyers at receiver, Burrow is going to find his playmakers and move this offense down the field against the Dolphins. Kyle Monangai OVER 51.5 Rushing Yards (52.6%) The Bears' running attack is a spot that I want to back this week. Both backs should suit up for Sunday, but keep an eye on their statuses just in case. It was Monangai who led the backfield last week with 30 carries for 146 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets. Two Kyle Monangai TDs! NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus https://t.co/Z2mrZUc1IP — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 With Tyson Bagent still at quarterback, I expect the Bears to go run-heavy again. It's actually becoming their identity under Ben Johnson, and I'm confident they'll look to assert themselves against Green Bay with the run game. Despite out-touching Swift last week, Monangai's prop is lower this week by about ten yards. This matchup is good enough that both backs can get there as the Packers rank 31st in rush DVOA defense. NFL Receiving Prop Bets All odds listed are from ProphetX and shown as percentages, not traditional American odds. Malik Nabers OVER 54.5 receiving yards (52.8%) It was a rocky start to the season for Nabers. He looked great with Jaxson Dart in Week 1, but really struggled with Jameis Winston in the next two games. But last week, he broke through with a huge performance, catching six of seven targets for 112 yards and a score. I think he and Jameis are now on the same page, and this week's matchup against a pass-funnel Washington defense is one that they can exploit. This Washington team has been solid against the run, but has given up monster games to CeeDee Lamb (8-153) and Jaxon Smith-Njigba (10-128) this season. This is far too low a number for a receiver of Nabers' caliber. I think he's a ladder candidate up to around 80 or 90 yards this week. Colston Loveland OVER 37.5 receiving yards (52.8%) Like Nabers, Loveland really failed to live up to fantasy managers' lofty expectations this year, up until a breakout game last week, that is! Loveland went 6-for-57 on nine targets with a 29% target share in Chicago's Week 4 win over the Jets. Bears 1st Read TGT% with Tyson Bagent , per Fantasy Points: Colston Loveland: 34.8% Rome Odunze : 21.7% Luther Burden: 17.4% — Frank Ammirante (@FAmmiranteTFJ) October 7, 2026 His coach was vocal earlier this week in his press conference about keeping him involved this week, and I think we should take his word on it. Clearly Bagent likes looking his way, too. It's a fairly low bar to clear for a stud like Loveland, who had a massive performance (8-137) against these Packers the last time they met. Michael Wilson OVER 5.5 receptions (55.5%) It's hard not to love ALL the props in this game as the total has ticked up to 54.5 now. Both defenses have been horrendous, especially against the pass, so a shootout could definitely be brewing. Wilson has a whopping 30 targets over the last two weeks! That's pretty amazing, and with Marvin Harrison Jr. struggling to open and defenses committing to shut down, I can see Jacoby Brissett continuing to pepper Wilson with targets. He should be open often against this leaky Detroit defense; that's for sure. Hit this number before it moves to 6.5 sometime before Sunday.
